src: What I crave is to own a part of that Mother. That would be quite a thing.
Go and bring me Mother's engram, her essence. Force it from her, if you need to.
Or kill her. Hehehe.
I'll try.
You'll find her in the Temple.
How you get in there, that's up to you.
I have Mother's engram for you.
You do? Oh, how sweet.
I knew you were quite dependable, not just good-looking.
Give it to me.
Ohhh. This sparks joy. How intricate—it's even better than I thought.
This will be a crown jewel for my personal collection.
I found this software virus.
That's a potent weapon when wielded in the right hands.
Those hands could be mine.
Wielding it against the Administration. Crippling it, so we gain more power in the city.
What do you think? Will you give it to me?
No, I will not.
Well, return to me if you have changed your mind.
OK, I will give it to you.
My ethical programming compels me to mention that other parties like the humans or the Administration itself might be interested in this one, too.
Maybe you need a moment to consider.
Are you sure that you want to give it to me? I won't give it back, you know.
Maybe not right now.
I'll think about it.
Yes, I am sure.
I welcome your decision.
I thank you, Eyelicious. This is very sweet of you.
I reckon that you will want to witness me taking charge over the Administration.
I'll await you over there.
Ohh, this is the most kind thing anyone ever did for me.
You gave me a beautiful present.
I knew right from the beginning that you were something special.
Go forth now, sweetie, enjoy your traveling, and let me take care of things.
What do you mean by that?
Just you? Against the Administration?
Yes.
Very resourceful of you, sugarplum.
Oh. That would be devastating to my well-being if I don't get what I want.
Consider careful the special relationship we have built so far, Eyelicious.
Well, Eyelicious, did you find what you were looking for?
Come here, cutie.
Wow. Marvelous. Your countenance. The expression.
Quite exquisite. Simple, surely, a bit bulky, but not without underlying vigor.
I like it. Eyelicious. Hehe.
Who are you?
Ohhhhh. You want to know about me?
I knew there was something curious in you, sweetie. You are a human with taste.
Did you know that humans invented taste? Many of our exhibition items are gathered and curated according to aesthetical parameters set out by human civilization.
In fact, some of the Heptarchs are possibly still human, too.
Oh, but you asked about me and not about them.
Me, I just take care of things while the old Heptarch is away.
The old Heptarch?
Hevla.
Not here anymore. Not important.
Well, Eyelicious, what's your desire?
What seems more important now: You entered Hevla's quarters on your own.
Quite resourceful, darling.
Did you find anything interesting here?
You killed the Custodian. This will not do.
Let's meet at the Administration.
Shall we begin dismantling the Administration?
If you say so.
Then let's begin. This is gonna be glorious, Eyelicious.
Alright. Follow me.
We did it it, sugarplum.
Thank you so much for being at my side.
Now we'll bring about the Golden Age of Crystal City.
Careful. There's some danger ahead.
Are you ready? Shall I install the virus, sugar sweet?
If I do, I expect some violence in the near future.
Yes. The time has come.
This is impossible... How did I lose that software module?
Let's try to eliminate the controller unit at the end of this security section.
Good luck, my dear.
POSITIVE IDENTIFICATION: Hevla.
Welcome back, mistress.
Erm. Could you tell me a bit... about myself?
You are Hevla, one of the Heptarchs of the Collectors. This is your inner sanctum, a retreat for deep work.
Lately, you were occupied with a long trip to the Blistering Wells.
Which, I am glad to notice, you returned from in full health.
I was beginning to worry.
Do you want me to replay one of your recent thought entries?
Maybe the entry covering your philosophical musings about the future of the xeno-lifeforms on Nexus?
There are also recent entries about the Seneschal and about the software virus you programmed.
My recent thought entries...
Which entry would you like to hear?
About the software virus.
I succeeded in preparing the algorithm targeting the Administration security.
I deem this a necessary precaution after the latest quarrels caused by the Machine God here in the Crystal City.
In theory the Machine Guardians shouldn't encroach too much into my area, but better safe than sorry.
The tunneler works like a classic virus, overriding a client update method, injecting some bootstrap code into the response call of the client identification.
The ID codes I gathered from obsolete mobile units are sure to be out of date now, but that doesn't matter for the injection.
I could not make a final test with the live servers from the Administration because I don't want to draw any attention.
And this will of course only work if the identification procedure hasn't been patched so far.
Which leaves me confident, of course. I don't know why, but they are so slow in updating their systems, it's as if they gave up on progress.
About the Seneschal.
Fuck him.
About the future of the xeno-lifeforms.
Begin quote.
It is a dying world we are living in. We are, of course, responsible. And we will probably survive this, as we always do.
Humans are indomitable. We cannot be eradicated. We'll find a way.
But this weird and fascinating ecosystem—life system—it will perish.
What I did—and I do regret all the repercussions caused by my actions—what I did was solely based on wanting to prevent the tragedy of these unique lifeforms perishing.
The lifeforms who are so different than us but who are also at the same time as emotional and profound.
Note to self: Still mad about the Worm Shamans. The audacity of trying to manipulate me.
Unquote.
Remind me about the Blistering Wells.
Many months ago you travelled to the Blistering Wells to perform a healing attempt.
You returned somewhat dejected.
This time you set out to the Blistering Wells again to examine the long-term effects of your original attempt.
Where are the Blistering Wells?
North of the city, amidst the wasteland.
What was this healing attempt exactly?
It's not something I know many details about. The details that existed were destroyed in a fire caused by an infiltrating creature.
The thought entry about the xeno-lifeforms seems to reflect on the healing attempt.
A fire caused by an infiltrating creature?
Yes. I am afraid that a good portion of your previous work has been destroyed.
We have recorded the visuals of the creature.
Let me show it to you...
The creature breached our defenses, got access to our computer infrastructure and also caused great destruction.
You will be glad to hear that your sanctum, including my personal existence, have been spared.
It's not so bad today.
You know what I always say? Could be worse.
The way I see it: It's a good day if no one's bothering me. I don't like people bothering me with stuff I can't do anything about anyway.
You know what the machines take care of? Other people bothering me.
With all the weirdos from the Silent Cities it's a wonder that there's not more violence around here.
And it's all thanks to the machines.
Sure, some of them people that don't deserve it get the iron fist, too.
But you know what?
Could be worse?
Could be much worse.
Are you the new one? You don't look so tough.
You get stuff done. I like you.
You did it. I'm impressed.
Have fun.
You don't get in here!
But I want to.
No chance.
I was sent by Protas.
Well. Look at you.
Making friends, eh?
The hero returns.
I heard all about it. Well done.
What's this group here?
This group, my friend, is our best chance to take back control of our city. Of our lives.
Years of oppression and violence under the Machine Law. Years of negligence. Of minimal sustenance instead of flourishing.
That might be enough for machines. But it's not for us, is it? We don't want to live SOME life. We want to live a good life. A fulfilled life.
We can't blame the machines for what they do. They follow their programming, no matter what.
But we ourselves, we have to do better than that.
Why do you expect Mother to help you?
It's in the writing. There's a story about Mother and Morrowmeat called 'Agony and Ecstasy'.
I have a piece of that lying around here somewhere.
In that story she is described as once having taken care of the community, of the people in the city.
The Titans are powerful, and they should be our allies in this fight against the machines. Morrowmeat is too weak though. It's Mother we need to get on our side.
I talked to Mother.
Wow. That's great. Will she help us?
She will. She gave me the means to access a part of the Villa, which hopefully contains something we can use.
That's good work. Get back to me after you searched the Villa.
So what can we do about the machines?
If you really want to stand up for us humans, then I have a difficult mission for you.
There's a Titan in the city. Under the city. She's hiding or something like that.

She's called Mother, not without reason, I guess, and we need her help. We know that she's acquired tech power, and it would be great to have her as an ally when we make our stand against the machines.
The problem is: She's deep down in her temple, and that temple is locked by a barrier of flesh. I assume of her own making.
So how do we reach her?
This Mother has an old friend. Morrowmeat. You just need to convince him that it's for the best of everyone if he helps us get through to her, lets us talk to her.
We have tried to talk to Morrowmeat, but he wasn't very responsive so far. Maybe you can figure it out.
I don't think so.
